analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible patch excerpt covers only the drain/stop section (new text on drain with coordinator disconnected: waits up to 10 s, finishes with no acknowledgement; shutdown waits up to 15 s per model unload and leaves a stuck native retirement to process exit) and a status/doctor paragraph about the enabled_models restart-needed notice. The excerpt is truncated, so the full patch was not seen. Units 8 and 9 (lines 1-804) are unchanged context for the listed hunks, which begin around head line 956.

I examined the visible text against the threat model and found no security regression. The doc changes describe existing behavior; no code, key custody, attestation, or authorization control is altered. The logout section (lines 533-582) matches the A-008 and T-053 model: it sends the token itself as a bearer to the recorded issuer, follows no redirects, confirms revocation only on 204, and states that offline logout is not remote invalidation. The cache section (lines 66-88) matches T-041: invalid or changed storage disables SSD caching, and no disk certification is claimed. The addon row (line 156) relates to TB-012 and T-059, but no hold-socket behavior is described here.

Integration questions: the 'no acknowledgement when the coordinator is disconnected' drain path depends on the code in ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown and ServiceDrain. That code was not supplied, so the claim that the disconnect already cancelled accepted work and that nothing queued can still reach the coordinator is unverified. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. The statement that a stuck native unload is left to process exit relates to T-028 (residual GPU data), but no behavior change is shown here.
